name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
summary: A unilateral free-weight pull performed with one knee and hand braced on a bench to build back thickness and lat strength.

setup: Place a dumbbell on the floor next to a flat bench.
Place your non-working knee and hand firmly on the bench, aligning the support hand directly under the shoulder.
Step the working-side foot out to the side and slightly back for stable three-point support, keeping the torso roughly parallel to the ground.
Reach down with a neutral grip to hold the dumbbell with your working arm fully extended.
steps: Initiate the movement by retracting your shoulder blade and driving your elbow back toward your hip.
Pull the dumbbell upward until the elbow passes the torso and the back muscles contract fully.
Pause briefly at the top without twisting your torso.
Lower the dumbbell under control back to a full dead-hang stretch before starting the next rep.
Complete all repetitions on one side before switching to the opposite arm.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you lower the weight into a full stretch; exhale forcefully as you row the dumbbell toward your hip.
cues: Lead with your elbow, not your hand.
Pull to your hip, not your armpit.
Keep your chest square to the bench.

common_faults.fault: Rotating the torso excessively to heave the weight up.
common_faults.correction: Keep your shoulders and hips parallel to the bench throughout the set; reduce the load if necessary.

common_faults.fault: Pulling straight up into the shoulder or chest using primarily the biceps.
common_faults.correction: Think of pulling the elbow backward toward the hip in a slight arc to emphasize the latissimus dorsi.

common_faults.fault: Cutting the bottom range of motion short.
common_faults.correction: Allow the scapula to protract slightly at the bottom for a full stretch before retracting and pulling.

precautions: Maintain a neutral spine and avoid rounding the lower back while supporting your weight.
